text:
Nathan MacKinnon is the rare star whose start needs no asterisk. He has 9 goals and 27 points in 17 games, shooting 14.8%, right around his normal, and the goals match his chances almost exactly (9 on 6.9 expected). There is nothing here to regress. If anything, his teammates have finished slightly below what he's set up for them.

That makes Colorado's uneven start more interesting than worrying. The Avalanche have won five of their last ten while MacKinnon keeps doing what he did in a 53-goal, Rocket Richard season. Evolving-Hockey had his impact on his team's chances in the 99th percentile among forwards in 2025-26, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 99th percentile both for chances from the slot and for setting up teammates. Corey Masisak of the Denver Post called the Oct. 28 win over New Jersey his best even-strength game of the season, with expected goals of 2.0 to 0.4.

Our range projects 105 to 137 points. What we'd watch is his ice time: 20.7 minutes a night is modest for a player this good, and more of it would mean more of everything.
headline: No asterisk needed in Colorado
